thread:
sophia: heads up — p95 on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate jumped ~400ms at ~15:20 UTC. digging the raw traces it looks like the quota limiter is queuing lots of requests and the dashboard percentiles are counting queue+service time which inflates the tail.
kevin: ugh yeah saw that. looks correlated with a quota refill hiccup in eu-west. queue_time spikes in the logs and KV cache hits steady.
maria: curious — do we want percentiles to include queue time or not? product uses dashboard p95 for SLOs so mixing queued time (which is tenant-local throttling) might be misleading.
alex: +1 we should surface both. idea: split the dashboard bar/legend into "queue_ms" vs "processing_ms" and show a stacked p50/p95/p99 breakdown. annotate when >10% of p95 is queue.
kevin: technical caveat: our current rollup pipeline only exports "latency_ms" as a single value. to separate we need the API to emit two tags: processing_ms and queued_ms (or one queued_ms metric). would be a small wire change.
sophia: Can we do a short-term workaround in the console without changing the API? e.g., use request_status tag to filter out requests that were throttled? not ideal because some throttled requests still get processed later.
maria: workaround is messy. better to add explicit queue_ms. proposal: add optional field in response metrics: "x-internal-queue-ms" (int). Default zero. Then ingest pipeline splits metrics into queue vs processing on ingestion and dashboards compute percentiles separately and stacked.
kevin: implementation notes:
```
// shim on limiter path
if (queued_ms > 0) add_response_metric("x-internal-queue-ms", queued_ms);
else add_response_metric("x-internal-queue-ms", 0);
```
In rollup: keep existing latency_ms for backward compat; add new histogram for queue_ms and processing_ms = latency_ms - queue_ms.
```
rollup.processing_hist.add(latency_ms - queue_ms)
rollup.queue_hist.add(queue_ms)
```
alex: console UX: add a toggle "attribute tail to queue vs runtime"; default off for legacy dashboards. show little tooltip: "Queue = time spent waiting at quota/limiter; Processing = time spent in runtime GPUs". Also show alert rule example: `when p95(queue_ms) > 50ms for 5m`.
sophia: any objections to API name? x-internal-queue-ms feels internal. Maybe `redwood.queue_ms` or `x-redwood-queue-ms`?
maria: prefer namespaced: `redwood.queue_ms`.
kevin: agree. also need ingestion change to drop negative processing_ms if we see latency < queue (shouldn't happen but safety check).
observability-bot: alert: "quota-refill-failure" triggered 15:19 UTC — affected 8 tenants. (automated)
sophia: next steps:
- kevin: PR to limiter to emit redwood.queue_ms (ETA tomorrow)
- kevin / infra: ingestion schema add queue_ms histogram mapping (rollout: canary then global)
- alex: console mockups for stacked percentiles + toggle (I'll drop mock in #design by EOD)
- maria: update SLO calc doc to clarify whether SLOs should include queue time (proposal: SLOs for product-facing latency should exclude queue_ms; infra SLOs include full latency)
kevin: will add a tiny flag `rollup.exclude_queued` so teams can opt into excluding queue when computing percentiles via query param.
sophia: great. could someone add a short example query we can drop into docs for "p95 excluding queued time"?
kevin: quick example (pseudo-SQL using rollups):
```
select percentile(95, processing_hist) from rollup where route = '/v1/generate' and time > now() - interval '5 minutes';
```
or prometheus-style if we export histograms separately:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_processing_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```
alex: I'll include the UI strings and quick query in the mock. if no one objects I'll merge the decision by EOD.
sophia: no objections from me. :thumbsup:
maria: sounds good. followup: can we add a tiny card in the dashboard that shows "queued rate" (# of requests that experienced queue > 0) to make it obvious when throttling is affecting tail?
kevin: yep that's trivial once queue_ms is in metrics.
sophia: thanks all — tagging @kevin @alex @maria for follow-ups. i'll file a short RFC in docs with the expected schema and SLO guidance.
alex: nice, i'll post mockups and include the alert rule examples. :rocket:
